title: Throwing a stoneware yunomi tea glass
subtitle: A tall, handleless stoneware drinking vessel in the Japanese yunomi tradition, fired to cone 6
excerpt: A yunomi is a tall, handleless stoneware tea glass used across East Asia for green tea and everyday drinking. At 90 mm tall and 70 mm in diameter, it throws quickly from 350 g of clay and suits a first or second throwing session. The absence of a handle means the finish work is straightforward. Glazed inside and on the upper half of the outside only, leaving the lower clay body bare.
sourceNotes: Yunomi tea glass throwing pattern derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Japanese handleless tea glass; tall, straight-sided, and slightly tapered at the base
The stage at which the form is stiff enough to trim a foot-ring without distorting
A trimmed ridge at the base that the yunomi rests on; gives a clean, lifted finish
First kiln firing to cone 06 (approx 1000 degrees C); makes greenware porous and ready for glaze
Pyrometric measure of heat-work in a kiln. Cone 06 approx 1000 degrees C; cone 6 approx 1220 degrees C

content.text: Silica dust is the chronic studio hazard. Silicosis is irreversible. Mix wet whenever possible. Wear a P100 respirator any time raw glaze powders are open. Wet-clean only: no sweeping, no dry sanding indoors.

Ensure adequate ventilation when firing: a downdraft vent or open window with an extractor. Wear welder's shade-5 glasses when peephole-watching at high temperatures. Do not open a hot kiln below 80 degrees C.
A
yunomi

is slightly tapered, widest at the rim and narrowing toward the base. The narrowing is subtle , 70 mm at the rim tapering to about 60 mm at the base. This shape suits the throwing mechanics well: walls that taper inward stay more stable than those that flare out. A trimmed
foot-ring
lifts the piece and is an essential part of the yunomi aesthetic.

materials.name: Mid-fire glaze, pre-mixed
materials.quantity: enough for inside and upper exterior

content.text: Centre, open, and pull
Wedge 350 g of smooth stoneware and centre on the wheel head.
Open a floor 45 mm in diameter, leaving 8 mm of clay at the base. Pull the walls upward in two to three passes, keeping the form vertical. Aim for 90 mm height and 70 mm rim diameter.
On the final pass, use the outside hand to bring the wall in very slightly at the base, creating a gentle inward taper from rim to base.

Smooth the rim with the chamois leather. Use the needle tool to level the rim if uneven , hold the needle lightly against the inside rim wall while the wheel turns slowly, then lift away the uneven clay above the cut line.
Wire off and allow to dry to
leather-hard
Trim the foot-ring
At leather-hard, centre the yunomi upside-down on the wheel head. Tap to centre: hold a finger lightly against the rim while spinning slowly and tap the base toward the centre until the wobble stops.

Use calipers to mark the foot-ring diameter , approximately 50 mm on a 60 mm base. Trim the foot-ring 5 mm tall and 5 mm wide using a loop tool. Remove clay from inside the foot-ring to match the wall thickness of the sides.
Smooth the foot-ring edges with a damp finger. Allow to reach bone-dry before bisque firing.
Bisque and glaze
Bisque fire to
bisque
at
cone
06 (approx 1000 degrees C).

Pour glaze inside the yunomi, swirl to coat, and pour out. Glaze the upper half of the outside to approximately 15 mm above the foot-ring. The lower half of the outside clay body is left bare , this is traditional for yunomi and protects against glaze runs adhering the piece to the kiln shelf.
Clean the foot-ring and base of all glaze. Glaze-fire to cone 6 (1220 degrees C).

rows.problem: Taper reversed , base wider than rim
rows.cause: The outside hand pushed outward rather than holding the wall in during the taper pass
rows.fix: On the final pull, consciously press inward at the base while allowing the rim to stay at full width.

rows.cause: Clay was too dry at trimming , the tool dragged and chipped rather than cut
rows.fix: Trim at true leather-hard: the clay should feel cool and firm but not hard. If too dry, mist the base and wait 10 minutes.
